findings.title: Pressure returns through paternal authority
findings.claim: The promised approach to the father carries the same pressure mechanism that earlier worked on Yusuf's guarded will, while the protected relation has changed to paternal custody.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 12:61:2 names an attempt to turn another's will, and the carrier at 12:61:4 supplies the immediate father whose permission controls the brother's movement. The strong same-surah returns at 12:23, 12:32, and 12:51 make the persuasion a recurring process of working on a guarded refusal; the global contact changes a flat assurance into an intended negotiation whose consent is still ahead.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the brothers' promise as an effort to work through a father's protective custody decision, with repeated approach and response rather than an already-won consent.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that they will try to persuade their father remains intact. The parallel does not equate the moral aims of the scenes, assert completed coercion here, or extend the father branch into an ancestor or source meaning.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run record supplies the three branch contacts and focus anchors, while exact strong same-surah connections independently return the pressure pattern and paternal stakes. Legacy reader formulations add relational detail without deciding the reading.

findings.claim: The emphatic promise to act later returns as agency bound by covenant, permission, and witness.
